solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Madam, a skirt will contain this material

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within its run of letters, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Someone tells a woman her skirt will be made of a certain fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a figured woven fabric, often silk or linen, used for tablecloths and furnishings.

clue.text: I'd flipped over, repose being most terrible

indicators.note: flipped over means turned the other way, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: the contraction of I had, written ID

explanation.surface: Someone flipped and found their lack of rest dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful or terrible, and this is its superlative form.

clue.text: What would excite them? Big heaven? It never came to pass

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so the letters of the words around it are mixed

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what would thrill people, before admitting it never happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excite' signals an anagram of THEM and BIG HEAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphenated noun for a thing that could have happened but did not, an unrealised possibility.

clue.text: Hard back

definitions.meaning: the rear part of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: The word means strict or severe as an adjective, and also the rear section of a ship as a noun.

clue.text: A maiden exploits charms

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over, one in which no runs are scored
to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: A young woman takes advantage of her attractions.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone and to entertain them pleasantly are near synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Fighting force initially might, it's likely, if trained in advance

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: An army might do well if it trains beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a military body of civilians raised to fight in an emergency.

clue.text: Take a previous, re-cooked, meat dish

indicators.note: re-cooked suggests something prepared again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reheat an earlier meal of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: This French dish is steak coated in crushed peppercorns, so it is a meat course.

clue.text: Remaining, not time for speaking

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation that follows is removed

explanation.surface: Staying on, but with no time to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying is the act of speaking or uttering words, a verb form used as a noun.

clue.text: A group of undesirables regularly goes wild

indicators.note: wild suggests things running out of control, so the letters of the two words before it are scrambled

explanation.surface: A band of ne'er-do-wells is said to go off the rails as a matter of habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but here it is simply part of the anagram fodder with 'goes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase originally named a police collection of criminals' photographs, and now means any collection of disreputable people.

clue.text: Tum suffering with gripes making one most irritable

indicators.note: suffering suggests something in a bad state, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A stomach ache leaves someone in a foul temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tum' is British slang for stomach and 'gripes' are stomach pains, so the surface is about indigestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumpy person is bad-tempered, so the superlative describes the crossest of all.

clue.text: Something wicked about Italian making protest

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the wickedness word goes round the short form for Italian

parts.note: a sin is a wicked act

explanation.surface: An Italian's wrongdoing provokes a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a form of protest in which demonstrators occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: Eccentric aunt with range of knowledge left on the shelf?

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters of the relative are rearranged

parts.note: ken means one's range of understanding, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: An odd, well-read aunt has never married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' rearranges AUNT into UNTA. 'Left on the shelf' usually means unmarried, but the question mark signals it is read literally: something on the shelf that no one has taken.
explanation.definitionFit: An item left on the shelf in a shop has not been picked up by anyone, so it remains unclaimed.

clue.text: A group's cash thrown into a stone box

indicators.note: thrown suggests things tossed about in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A club's funds are tossed into a stone chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarcophagus is a stone coffin, usually carved, so a box made of stone.

clue.text: Tea awfully dear — it's a travesty

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of the next word are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the tea is so bad it is a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, and a travesty is a ridiculous imitation, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Classes of people left out of grand buildings

indicators.note: out of here means taken away from, so the letter for left is removed

explanation.surface: Some social groups are excluded from stately homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Castes are hereditary social classes, most famously in the Hindu system.

clue.text: Rubbish in plot upset gentleman turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the letters climb, so the title is read backwards

parts.note: sir is the address or title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman finds a garden plot wrecked and full of litter.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered rubbish or wreckage left after destruction.

clue.text: Girl in time seen to be ordinary?

indicators.note: in places the girl's name within the word for a period of time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A girl in a period setting looks plain and unremarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Average describes something typical or middling, which is what ordinary means as an adjective.

clue.text: That group of map-makers featured in article

indicators.note: featured in means appearing within, so the map-makers sit inside the article

parts.note: the is the definite article in grammar
OS is the Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency

explanation.surface: A cartographers' society appears in a magazine piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points to a set of people or things already identified, the plural of that.

clue.text: Liking decorum

definitions.meaning: good judgement in what is seemly or proper

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a preference as well as a sense of propriety, as in good manners.

clue.text: Hearts broken with poverty — expect no more fun

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters of the two words are reassembled

explanation.surface: Heartbroken and poor, someone is told the good times have ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearts broken' reads as heartbreak, but 'broken' is the anagram signal working on HEARTS plus POVERTY.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom announces that a period of enjoyment has come to an end, so no more good times lie ahead.

clue.text: Entertainer, one who got things stitched up!

definitions.meaning: a vocalist performs for an audience

definitions.text: one who got things stitched up!
definitions.meaning: Isaac ... founded the famous sewing machine company, so the name suggests stitching

explanation.surface: A performer who once sewed things up for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitched up' usually means framed; here it is literal sewing, via the sewing machine maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocal performer entertains people, and the sewing-machine brand name brings in the stitching sense.

clue.text: Ball game in uniform aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means on a vessel, so the word for uniform goes inside the ship's letters

explanation.surface: Someone plays a ball game in uniform on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing, or NATO's U; here it means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is rugby union played with seven players a side, a fast ball game with its own tournaments.
